messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that repairs Java 8 code so that it correctly solves the given programming problem. The code reads and writes I/O from the console.

samples.content:
<repaired_code>
import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class bubblestrike {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        String[] parts = br.readLine().trim().split("\\s+");
        int N = Integer.parseInt(parts[0]);
        double P = Double.parseDouble(parts[1]);
        
        int lo = 0, hi = N;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
            if (satisfiesCondition(mid, N - mid, P)) {
                hi = mid;
            } else {
                lo = mid + 1;
            }
        }
        System.out.println(lo);
    }

    private static boolean satisfiesCondition(int good, int bad, double limit) {
        int total = good + bad;
        if (total < 3) return false;
        
        // Total number of ways to choose 3 maps from total maps
        long totalWays = (long)total * (total - 1) * (total - 2) / 6;
        
        // Count favorable outcomes where at least one of the selected maps is among the "good" ones
        // and Johnny can pick it (considering the game rules)
        
        // Actually, let's think about the probability more carefully:
        // The system selects 3 maps randomly from N maps.
        // Johnny studies 'good' maps, opponents don't know him and pick randomly.
        // Each player picks one map to discard from the 3 shown.
        // The game is played on a map that was NOT picked by either player.
        // If both players pick different maps to discard, the remaining map is played.
        // If both pick the same map to discard, one of the other two is randomly selected.
        
        // We need the probability that the played map is one Johnny studied.
        
        // Let's enumerate all possible scenarios:
        // Case 1: All 3 maps are studied (good maps) -> probability = C(good,3)/C(total,3)
        //   - Johnny will pick one of the 3 to discard
        //   - Opponents pick randomly among 3
        //   - If opponents pick same as Johnny (1/3 chance), one of remaining 2 is randomly chosen -> 2/3 chance to get a good map
        //   - If opponents pick different (2/3 chance), the remaining map is played -> 100% good
        //   - Overall: 1/3 * 2/3 + 2/3 * 1 = 2/9 + 2/3 = 8/9
        
        // Case 2: Exactly 2 good maps, 1 bad map -> probability = C(good,2)*C(bad,1)/C(total,3)
        //   - Johnny will pick the bad map to discard (optimal strategy)
        //   - Opponents pick randomly among 3
        //   - If opponents pick bad map (1/3), remaining 2 good maps -> Johnny picks one, system randomly picks one of remaining 2 -> 100% good
        //   - If opponents pick one good map (2/3), remaining maps are 1 good and 1 bad -> Johnny picks bad, so good map is played -> 100% good
        //   - Actually, if opponents pick different maps, the remaining map is played. If they pick same, one of other two randomly.
        //   - Let's be more precise:
        //     * Johnny picks bad map (1 choice)
        //     * Opponent 1 picks randomly among 3, Opponent 2 picks randomly among 3
        //     * If both opponents pick bad map (1/3 * 1/3 = 1/9): system randomly picks one of the 2 good maps -> 100% good
        //     * If one picks bad, one picks good (2 * 1/3 * 2/3 = 4/9): remaining map is good -> 100% good
        //     * If both pick good maps (2/3 * 2/3 = 4/9): 
        //         - If they pick same good map (2 * 1/3 * 1/3 = 2/9 of the 4/9 = 1/2 of 4/9 = 2/9): system randomly picks one of remaining 2 (1 good, 1 bad) -> 50% good
        //         - If they pick different good maps (2/3 * 1/3 = 2/9 of the 4/9 = 1/2 of 4/9 = 2/9): remaining map is bad -> 0% good
        //     * Actually, let's recalculate: Opponent 1 and 2 each independently pick one of 3 maps.
        //       Total 9 equally likely outcomes.
        //       Johnny picks bad map.
        //       Outcomes:
        //         (bad,bad): remaining {good1, good2}, system picks randomly -> 100% good
        //         (bad,good1): remaining {good2}, 100% good
        //         (bad,good2): remaining {good1}, 100% good
        //         (good1,bad): remaining {good2}, 100% good
        //         (good1,good1): remaining {good2, bad}, system picks randomly -> 50% good
        //         (good1,good2): remaining {bad}, 0% good
        //         (good2,bad): remaining {good1}, 100% good
        //         (good2,good1): remaining {bad}, 0% good
        //         (good2,good2): remaining {good1, bad}, system picks randomly -> 50% good
        //       So favorable outcomes: 6 out of 9 give 100% good, 2 out of 9 give 50% good, 1 out of 9 gives 0% good.
        //       Probability = 6/9 * 1 + 2/9 * 0.5 + 1/9 * 0 = 6/9 + 1/9 = 7/9
        
        // Case 3: Exactly 1 good map, 2 bad maps -> probability = C(good,1)*C(bad,2)/C(total,3)
        //   - Johnny will pick the bad map that is less likely to be played (but since opponents pick randomly, he should pick one bad map)
        //   - Actually, optimal strategy: pick one of the bad maps to discard.
        //   - Let's enumerate: Johnny picks bad1.
        //     Outcomes for opponents:
        //       (bad1,bad1): remaining {bad2, good}, system picks randomly -> 50% good
        //       (bad1,bad2): remaining {good}, 100% good
        //       (bad1,good): remaining {bad2}, 0% good
        //       (bad2,bad1): remaining {good}, 100% good
        //       (bad2,bad2): remaining {bad1, good}, system picks randomly -> 50% good
        //       (bad2,good): remaining {bad1}, 0% good
        //       (good,bad1): remaining {bad2}, 0% good
        //       (good,bad2): remaining {bad1}, 0% good
        //       (good,good): remaining {bad1, bad2}, system picks randomly -> 0% good
        //     Probability = 2/9 * 1 + 2/9 * 0.5 = 2/9 + 1/9 = 3/9 = 1/3
        
        // Case 4: 0 good maps -> probability = 0
        
        // Let's compute the overall probability:
        // P = C(good,3)/C(total,3) * 8/9 + C(good,2)*C(bad,1)/C(total,3) * 7/9 + C(good,1)*C(bad,2)/C(total,3) * 1/3
        
        long case1 = (long)good * (good - 1) * (good - 2) / 6;
        long case2 = (long)good * (good - 1) / 2 * bad;
        long case3 = (long)good * bad * (bad - 1) / 2;
        
        double prob = (case1 * 8.0 + case2 * 7.0 + case3 * 3.0) / (totalWays * 9.0);
        
        return prob >= limit;
    }
}
